The other 61 numbers need no individual record: each is carried only by actors whose death reaches SetDungeonKillFlag through the default routing, and has no consumer except the spawn check (several of them are still reused by other dungeons: see the table) (table in FL14_20261031_table.md). D6.name: dungeon enemy kill
D6.lifecycle: Bytes $0A80-$0A9F of the save block (flag $0400 + enemy number; byte $0A80 + (n >> 3), bit n AND 7). Zeroed by ClearAllWramFlags (WorldMapController entry {238336}, st68_kara {438261}, sp58_red_eye {426502} only when $0AA6 = 2), by the inline loop of game_over_sequence {54988}-{55002} on a real game over (gems < 100; a revive keeps the bits) and at boot. ClearSceneState zeroes only $0A00-$0A01, so ordinary scene changes keep the bits: a number reused by two scenes of one visit is one shared bit, and a number reused by the next dungeon is a stale bit unless a reset ran between the dungeons. Each dungeon numbers its enemies from about $01, so 241 of the 253 numbers appear in several scenes.
D6.access: COP $D8 SetDungeonKillFlag (StandardEnemyDefeatHandler {56306}, EnemyDefeatDispatch {697510}, awB1_wall_walker {770381}, pyCC_mystic_ball {771937}; all reach SetWramFlag {44172}), CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag at spawn ({249721}), one direct reader (gw88_tomb_dark_space {507380}, $0A9F) and the two clearing sites. No COP flag operand and no other helper call reaches $0400-$04FF.

Full record because: several rows in one session, tomb mask byte $0A9F, actor that may skip or never write the bit. pyD2_haunt: OrExtraFlags #$0090 (pyD2_haunt.asm:211 {770788}) includes the boss bit $0080, so the StandardEnemyDefeatHandler path skips the kill bit. Bit 5 of $0A9F is tested by gw88_tomb_dark_space (gw88_tomb_dark_space.asm:18 {507380}): the low byte of $0A9F equals $3F only when $F8-$FD are all set and $FE-$FF are clear. The name is a slot name (enemy number), not derived from dialog text.

meanings.summary: The enemy with number $FE (flag index $04FE) has been defeated since the last reset of the kill bits; scene load skips every spawn record that carries this number.

effects.set: InitActorFromSceneData frees the slot of every enemy spawn record with this number (CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag carry set), does not count it in enemiesRemaining and swaps the record's event-block tiles
effects.clear: Every spawn record with this number spawns its actor normally and the actor is counted in enemiesRemaining.
